info.title: LogB
info.description:
The HTTP API behind LogB, served under `/api`.

Two credentials work everywhere except token management: the `logb_session` cookie a browser gets from `POST /auth/login`, and an `Authorization: Bearer logb_pat_...` token for clients that are not browsers. A client obtains its first token by logging in interactively once and calling `POST /auth/tokens`; token management deliberately refuses bearer credentials, so a leaked token cannot mint replacements.

**Writing offline.** `POST /objects/{id}/activities` and `POST /objects/{id}/attachments` accept a `client_op_id`: any string unique to the write, generated once by the client and kept across every retry. The server records it under a unique index, so replaying a write whose response was lost resolves to the row already created instead of duplicating it. Any client that queues writes while offline should use it.

This document is checked against the running router by `tests/openapi.rs`: a route added, removed or renamed without updating it fails the build.

get.summary: Liveness probe. The only route needing no credential.
Whether the instance still needs its first (admin) user.

post.summary: Create the first user. Refused once any user exists.
Exchange credentials for a session cookie. Rate limited per IP.
End every session of this account, this one included.

get.summary: The signed-in user.
List this user's API tokens. Never includes the token itself.

post.summary: Issue an API token. The plaintext is in this response and nowhere else, ever: only a hash is stored. Requires a session cookie, never a bearer token.

delete.summary: Revoke a token. Takes effect on its next request.

get.summary: Every object owned by this user.
One object.

patch.summary: Replace an object. Every field except `cover_attachment_id` is a full replace: a field left out is written as null, so send the object whole. `cover_attachment_id` is three-state — absent keeps the cover, null clears it, an id sets it.

delete.summary: Delete an object with its activities, reminders and attachments. The files and blobs they referenced deliberately survive until the retention purge.

get.summary: Cost and consumption rollups for one object.
Up to 20 recent, distinct activity titles for this object, for repeat suggestions.
One page of the object's timeline, newest first. `X-Total-Count` carries the unpaged total. `limit` is clamped to 500 rather than refused.

X-Total-Count.description: Matching rows in total, ignoring the page window

post.summary: Log an activity. Send `client_op_id` to make a retry idempotent.

200.description: This `client_op_id` was already recorded; the existing row is returned

get.summary: One activity, with its attachments.

patch.summary: Replace an activity. A full replace, as with objects.

delete.summary: Delete an activity and its attachments.

get.summary: Files attached to this object.

post.summary: Upload a file, optionally onto one activity. Identical bytes are stored once and shared. Send `client_op_id` to make a retry idempotent.

delete.summary: Detach a file. The stored bytes are reclaimed once nothing references them and the tombstone has aged out of the sync window.

get.summary: The original bytes. Served from this origin under a sandbox policy; only a short list of types renders in place, everything else downloads.
A thumbnail, for image attachments.
Reminders for one object.

post.summary: Create a reminder, due on a date, a counter reading, or both.

get.summary: Everything due now, plus anything coming due within `within_days`. A snoozed reminder appears in neither until its snooze lapses.
One reminder.

post.summary: Mark done, optionally against the activity that did it. A repeating reminder schedules its successor from that point.
Suppress a reminder for `days`, without touching its real due date.

delete.summary: Clear a snooze, making the reminder due again immediately.

get.summary: Objects and activities matching `q`.
Instance settings.
Everything this user owns as a zip: JSON plus the original files. Streamed.

post.summary: Restore an export. Adds to what is there; it does not replace it.

get.summary: Every user. Admin only.

patch.summary: Change a user's password or language. Anyone may change their own; only an admin may change anyone else's. A password change ends every session AND revokes every API token of that account.

delete.summary: Delete a user with everything they own. Admin only.

post.summary: Apply a batch of offline ops with field-level last-write-wins.
post.description: Every op in the batch is applied inside one transaction, so a client that retries after a lost response finds either all of its ops recorded or none. `results` is positional: `results[i]` describes `ops[i]`. An op that loses the last-write-wins comparison is `superseded` -- recorded in the change feed, but not written to the row; only a malformed or unauthorised op is `rejected`. Replaying a `client_op_id` already in the log reports `accepted` without applying it a second time.

get.summary: Page through the change feed from a cursor.
get.description: `since` is the `next_seq` from the previous call, or 0 for a first pull. `complete` is false when the page filled exactly, meaning the client should pull again immediately with the returned `next_seq`. A `since` older than the server's retention horizon -- including a non-zero `since` against a log that has been purged empty -- answers 410 instead of a silently-incomplete 200; the client must re-bootstrap from a fresh export rather than trust an incremental catch-up. A non-zero `since` also requires `epoch` to match the database's current one -- see the `epoch` parameter -- or the same 410 is returned.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: The cursor to resume after: the `next_seq` from a previous pull, or 0 for a first pull.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of changes to return. Clamped to [1, 1000].

parameters.name: epoch
parameters.description: The `epoch` from a previous pull or bootstrap, proving which database `since` was issued against. Required whenever `since` is non-zero; a mismatched or missing epoch answers 410, the same as a stale `since`, because a restored database reissues `changes.seq` for entirely different ops.

410.description: `since` predates the retained history; re-bootstrap instead of resuming.

get.summary: The full snapshot a new device starts from, or that a stale device falls back to.
get.description: Every live (non-tombstoned) row the caller owns, across every syncable table, plus `seq` -- the cursor to resume incremental pulls from -- and `server_time`. `seq` is read before the rows are, so an op landing between the two reads is, at worst, delivered again by the first `GET /sync/pull`; the apply path is idempotent, so that is harmless. This is the only read path that returns `client_uuid` for existing rows, so a device must bootstrap before it can push anything that references them. Used both by a brand-new device and by one whose cursor is older than the retention horizon, after `GET /sync/pull` answers 410.

bearerToken.description: An API token from `POST /auth/tokens`. Does not expire; revoke it to end it.

prefix.description: The first characters of the token, for recognition only

last_used_at.description: Recorded at most once a day

token.description: The plaintext, readable only in this response

cost_cents.description: Money is always integer cents; never a float

quantity_milli.description: Fuel quantity in thousandths of `fuel_unit`; fuel activities only

client_op_id.description: Generated once per write and kept across retries; makes a replay idempotent

due.description: Due now, accounting for any live snooze

days_until.description: Against the real due date, snooze or not

client_op_id.description: Unique per op; replaying one is a no-op.

field.description: Required for `set`; must be a syncable column of `entity`.

value.description: The new value for `set`. Its shape must match the target column: a string for a text column, an integer for an integer column, or null to clear it -- a boolean is rejected everywhere, and any other mismatch (e.g. a string into an integer column) comes back `rejected` rather than being coerced.

edited_at.description: RFC3339. Canonicalised to UTC milliseconds before it is compared.

device_id.description: Breaks ties on equal `edited_at`; the greater string wins.

results.description: One entry per op, in the order the ops were sent.

ids.description: client_uuid to the server's integer id, for references a client only knows by uuid.

seq.description: The monotonic pull cursor. Pass the last row's `seq` back as `since` to resume.

field.description: Null for `create` and `delete`; only a `set` names a field.

value.description: Double-encoded JSON: this string is itself the JSON-serialized form of the value that was set, so a string value arrives as e.g. `"\"Golf VII\""` and a client must `JSON.parse` it to recover the real value. Null here is ambiguous by construction: an explicit `value: null` on a `set` (clearing the field) is stored as SQL NULL and is indistinguishable from a `create`/`delete` row, which never carries a value at all.

next_seq.description: Pass as `since` on the next call.

complete.description: False when the page filled exactly; the client should pull again immediately.

epoch.description: Which database these seq numbers belong to. A client stores it beside its cursor and passes it back as the `epoch` query parameter on its next pull.

objects.description: Every live row from `objects`, verbatim, keyed by column name.

activities.description: Every live row from `activities` whose object is also live.

reminders.description: Every live row from `reminders` whose object is also live.

attachments.description: Every live row from `attachments` whose object is also live.

files.description: Every live row from `files`, verbatim, keyed by column name.

seq.description: Pass as `since` on the first `GET /sync/pull` call.

epoch.description: Which database this snapshot came from. Pass alongside `seq` as the `epoch` query parameter on the first `GET /sync/pull` call.
